cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've borrowed five thousand for the charity auction advance. Record it as a commitment, not a shortfall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only your mum registered, and she's just giving us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll bid. A commitment must be honoured; separate that from attendance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If we borrow more to buy our own prizes, we'll owe both loans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two loans, one donation. Please stop counting the donation twice. Increase the card limit and I can balance the sheet.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commitment classification and A3 separation of attendance give A an expert sales method, but A5 corrects an error B did not make.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no bidders causes A3 self-bidding; B4 two loans is answered by A5 falsely attributing double donation counting.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 are sensible objections to A debt plan and should not need to become bad accountants for the scene.

heightening.evidence: A5 increases the card limit but the claimed balancing does not actually answer B4 loans.

specificity.evidence: A1 charity advance and B4 duplicate debts establish a coherent disaster before the false correction.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 counting twice phrase supplies an unearned professional victory.
